finding: apps/api/src/app.ts:640 — one failed read on the stream sends `unreadable` and returns, so the page stops following a running session until a reload; the /transcript 502 is untested

finding: apps/api/src/app.ts:513 — every read calls `e.view` only to learn `settled`, which observes every harness; with `e.transcript`'s own observe that is two `claude agents` calls a second per open stream

why: Took neither suggested option; I removed the rule instead. `parentOf(e, id)` checks git first (every result branch still exists and is on the base branch), then asks `decision`, the function behind the parent's own `wf decide`. A running parent with nothing committed still doesn't ship, which is what the old rule was for; a finished one with no commit does, and its child starts. Because `decision` answers `cancelled` first, a cancelled parent never ships even when merged (the request's 'it will never ship'), and `afterRefusal` always refuses one. Side effect: a branch merged while its run still runs waits for the run to finish. Also: `gated(run)` in run.ts decides whether any parent is read; `parentRecord` (record and git only) feeds `wf start`; `parentsOf` replaces `parentReader`. New store test: a parent signs off with no commit past its base → its `wf decide` says shipped, the child's next tick files its roots, and `wf start --after` it is accepted; it fails with the old rule put back. The first store test now also merges while the parent still runs (nothing filed) and releases the child only after sign-off; the cancelled-parent test merges and still files nothing. Parent and child share one fake engine board in the tests.

finding: apps/api/src/builder.ts:284: the PUT writes whatever draft it is sent with no check that the folder is still what the draft started from, so a step added or edited by hand while the builder is open is deleted or written over on Save.

why: Commit 6409aa2 fixes the concrete part. The record is now `QueueTry { at, text, repo, why, refused }`, where `refused` means exitCode 2, the package's own refusal. Only a refusal lasts, and `nextQueued(listing, repo)` passes over a card only while both its text and the repository it would be tried on match; a card with no `repo:` refused because `wf up` ran in the wrong repository is tried again from the right one. Any other failure, such as git failing on the repository, is tried again on the next pass, where the card keeps its place. If it fails the same way on the same repository, it is marked `again`, not rewritten, and `wf up` doesn't repeat it; `wf inbox` shows `failed at <time>: <why> — not a refusal`. Tests in test/queue-store.test.ts: a queued card whose repo folder has no git fails with git's words, is tried on every pass while the card behind waits, is said once over two passes of `wf up`, and starts once git is there; a card with no `repo:` refused on a repository without its workflow is passed over there and started from one that has it. Five mutations each fail a test. I kept the policy of passing over a refused card rather than retrying it every pass. Read literally, one card per pass means a refused card would log every 4 seconds and block the queue for good, and I believe the brief's 'no hot loop' was about avoiding exactly that. `$WF_ROOT/queue/` is the only level-triggered place to remember a try: the card file belongs to the person, and the tick must carry nothing in memory between passes. The reviewer asked a person to confirm this reading; it is written in features.md and the commit message, and stopping the queue at a refused card instead is one line in `nextQueued`. Left in features.md: restoring a missing workflow doesn't un-skip a refused card, and a card that keeps failing without a refusal holds the queue behind it.

The gap is removed from features.md's 'What it leaves'.

finding: apps/web/src/lib/asks.ts:83 — a step that signed off blocked past its budget reads `over budget`, so `offersOf` gives it only a RaiseRow with no answer box and no recheck for a refused check; the answer is lost once the raise is asked; nothing tests a blocked or unsigned step past its budget
why:
Agreed: `answerLines` offers `--budget --message` for this case, and `retryable` keeps `recheck` for a refused check.

The api's `StepRaise` now also carries the package's `modes` (from `retryable`) and `own` (from `ownStatus`), since an `over budget` word no longer says how the step ended. `offersOf` offers the raise wherever the api carries one. That also covers a check that did not finish past its budget, with its recheck chosen first; before, its try-again row had no amount box, so a new session of it could only be refused.

`RaiseRow` gains a box for what to tell the try. When `own` is `blocked`, the row shows the question, the box is the answer, and 'Raise the budget and answer' stays disabled until one is written, the same rule as the answer row. Where `recheck` is among the modes, the row offers it; choosing it closes the amount and message boxes and sends `{mode:'recheck'}` alone.

Tests:
- `apps/api/test/budget.test.ts` adds a run with a blocked step and a refused check, each past its budget. It checks `raise.modes`/`own` and `wf decide`'s answering line; that an answer without a raise, or a raise not above the spend, is a 409 carrying `retry()`'s refusal verbatim; that answer and raise on one ask is a 202 with both on the ask file; and that a recheck with no budget is a 202.
- `asks.test.ts` and `components.test.ts` cover the blocked row (answer box, disabled button), a refused check (recheck radio) and an unfinished check (recheck first, boxes closed).
- The e2e seed gains `palette`, blocked past a $1 budget. The cost page checks its answer box and that the button waits for an answer; the check exits 0.

Unsigned past a budget is covered in `asks.test.ts` only: making it in the api needs a closeout schema on the filed task, and it takes the same optional-message path as a refused check.

finding: apps/api/src/workflows.ts:184 — POST /api/runs accepts a start from any website (body parsed whatever its content-type, no Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site check), and main.ts binds every interface
why: Confirmed first: a text/plain POST to the machine's outward address got 201 and wrote a run. Separate tests show the board's start through the proxy and a curl-style start both get 201, and a main.test.ts test confirms nothing answers on the outward IPv4 address. vite.config.ts and the e2e now use 127.0.0.1 by number. In a real browser, a JSON POST from another localhost port got through vite preview's default CORS and reached the api, where only the Sec-Fetch-Site check refused it; the board's own start still got 201. Evidence is in artifacts/implement/start-guard.md. GET routes are still exposed to DNS rebinding; I left them alone because the finding concerns the one write.
